messages:
annie: FYI seeing a sustained increase in 429 spikes for org=acme over the last ~3h. Not huge per-key, but org-level 429 rate jumped to ~12% during bursts. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc/quotas

evie: copying in SRE. Is this the per-org quota being enforced as a hard cap or a burst window?

annie: looks like hard enforcement at the org layer. Per-key limits remain under threshold. Logs show many concurrent keys under same org sending short bursts.

sanjay: probable cause = token-bucket at org scope drained by many keys at once. We allow more burst at key-level but org-level has small bucket. We should consider a short-term mitigation + telemetry changes.

ingrid: agree. Can we add an alert that triggers on org-aggregate 429 ratio and concurrent unique keys? e.g. when 429_rate(org) > 5% AND uniq_keys_active(org) > 50 within 5m.

annie: that would help reduce noisy alerts. Also want a panel that shows 'headroom' for orgs: (org_capacity - recent_rps).

evie: suggested alert PromQL for reference:
```
sum(rate(responses_total{status="429",scope="org"}[5m])) by (org)
/ sum(rate(requests_total{scope="org"}[5m])) by (org) > 0.05
```
Combine with: `increase(distinct_keys[5m]) > 50` as a second cond in our alertmanager.

annie: +1. Also add a related alert for 429_spike_count > baseline*3 to catch sudden bursts.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-033 - high org 429 rate (acme). PagerDuty notified to team oncall.

cs-bot: auto message to CS: "Heads up — ACME seeing quota 429s this morning. We're triaging; reaching out if you have customer context."

sanjay: short-term mitigation options:
- widen org bucket size by 2x for 15m for ACME (rate-limiter change)
- apply per-key smoothing so single keys can't drain org bucket by themselves
- route lower-priority requests to a cached response path / smaller model
Which should we try first?

evie: prefer non-invasive first: add per-key smoothing + route idle or telemetry-only traffic to cache. Widening bucket is disruptive (can mask true over-usage).

annie: agree with evie. Also want to push an X-RateLimit-Warn header so clients get early warning. We can add a soft-threshold that emits header at 75% org usage.

zach: I can pick up the header + console UX to show per-org headroom and soft-limit warnings. Will add a console flag to enable soft-limits for specific customers.

ingrid: for long-term: we should expose an "org burst profile" in the console (burst capacity, refill rate, effective per-key share) and let customer choose between more burst vs stricter smoothing. This reduces CS tickets.

annie: runbook steps for this incident (draft):
1) Verify 429 spike org-aggregate in Grafana and validate with raw logs (loki query).
2) Identify top 10 keys contributing to requests in 5m window.
3) If top keys are internal test bots -> throttle them.
4) If many legitimate keys -> enable per-key smoothing + route low-priority model.
5) Notify CS + customer with mitigations and ETA.
6) Monitor for 30m then revert temp changes if stable.

sanjay: Loki query for step 2:
```
{env="prod"} | json | org="acme" | topk(10, sum by (api_key) (rate(requests_total[5m])))
```

annie: I'm opening a Grafana panel PR to add the headroom and uniq-key heatmap. Will also create an alert rule based on evie's promql and the distinct-key condition.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: changelist 6432 pushed to staging: rate-limiter: add soft-header + per-key smoothing flag.

evie: thanks. once in staging, run the ACME synthetic load for a few burst patterns to validate we don't create new regressions (latency, tail p95).

zach: on console UX — proposal: under 'Quotas' show a small graph: '30m headroom' + 'expected time to refill' + a toggle to enable soft-warnings. Also add an exportable playbook link.

annie: can someone update the SRE playbook doc with the new Grafana links + runbook? I'll reference it in the incident.

ingrid: I'll add a short blurb for CS to send a templated message offering "soft-limit" opt-in while we stabilize.

cs-bot: CS notified ACME success@acme.example. Waiting reply.

annie: thanks all — next actions: zach add console flag PR, me add grafana/alert PR, evie run staging tests, ingrid craft CS template. We'll reconvene in 30m.

sanjay: one more thought for postmortem: consider adaptive org buckets that scale based on recent cardinality. Could reduce manual fiddling.

annie: noted. Adding as follow-up item in the incident ticket.

zach: PR for console flag created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1578

annie: PR for grafana panels/alerts: https://grafana-repo/pulls/422 and created INC-2026-033 in our incident tracker.

cs-bot: ACME replied: "We had one of our worker fleets run a wide restart and flooded requests while warming. We'll throttle on our side too."

annie: closing loop — we'll keep soft-limit enabled for 1 hour then revert unless further issues. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
